## Same Model, Different Work

- Chatbot (~2022) — one question in, one answer out, done
- Deep Research — a topic in, a cited report out, dozens of pages read
- Claude Code — a bug report in; edit, test, re-edit until green

\vspace{2mm}

**Same model on every side. What differs is the program around it.**

<!-- 훅: 셋 다 같은 모델. 차이는 모델 밖 프로그램 — 여기서 수업 전체가 출발 -->

## The LLM Call

- Text in → text out. **No other channel.**
- Cannot open a file, run a search, verify its own output
- Produces plausible tokens — not actions on the world

\vspace{2mm}

Everything the model cannot do → **code outside the model**

## Control Flow

**Control flow** = which action next · repeat? · stop?

\vspace{2mm}

- **Workflow** — control flow fixed in advance, by code
- **Agent** — control flow decided by the model's output

\vspace{2mm}

Criterion: the **location of decision authority** — not capability
\newline (*Building Effective Agents*, Anthropic 2024)

## The Criterion, Applied

Same search feature, two systems:

\vspace{2mm}

- Fixed pipeline: translate → summarize → store (search inside) → **workflow**
- Assistant that decides *whether* to search, and *with what query* → **agent**

\vspace{2mm}

Having a capability ≠ deciding. **Deciding makes the agent.**

## Workflow versus Agent

![](figures/fig-1-1-loop-vs-workflow.png){width=88%}

## The Agent Loop

1. Model reads the input so far → generates output
2. Code interprets: action → execute · final answer → stop
3. Result appended to the input
4. Back to 1

\vspace{2mm}

Deep Research and Claude Code: same skeleton, different tools. (Built by hand — Ch. 4)

## The Loop, Watched Live

A Claude Code session, on screen:

- a line of judgment — *"tests fail in parse_date; regex misses 2-digit years"*
- a tool call — edit the file, run the tests
- the result — pass/fail log, appended
- repeat, until green or the attempt cap

\vspace{2mm}

That transcript **is** the loop — running in a shipped product.

<!-- 시연 포인트: 실제 Claude Code/Cursor 화면을 여기서 잠깐 보여주기 -->

## Components

| Component | Why it exists |
|:--|:--|
| Model | decides, through its output |
| Instructions | the goal, the permissions |
| Tools | text alone changes nothing |
| Memory / Context | each step builds on the last |

\vspace{2mm}

Four parts, every framework, every week's lab. (Ch. 2 · 3 · 9–10)

## Autonomy — a Matter of Degree

| Level | Example | LLM decides |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Fixed pipeline | translate → summarize | nothing |
| Router | triage inquiries | one branch |
| Bounded loop | edit until tests pass | iterate · stop |
| Autonomous | "research this topic" | the plan |

\vspace{2mm}

A trade: flexibility ↔ predictability, cost

## Real Systems on the Spectrum

![](figures/fig-1-2-autonomy-spectrum.png){width=96%}

## Case — Deep Research

- OpenAI (2025) · Gemini (2024) · Perplexity
- In: one topic. Out, minutes later: a cited report
- The model decides: which searches, which pages, when enough
- Delegated form: assign → review the deliverable

\vspace{2mm}

Note for Ch. 7: these products write a **plan** first — some let you edit it.

## Case — Coding Agents

- Claude Code (terminal) · Cursor (IDE) · Devin (delegated) · Copilot (embedded)
- The bounded loop, productized: edit → test → read failure → edit
- Guardrails live in **code**: permission prompts, attempt caps
- Same model as the chat products — the loop and tools differ

## Case — Support Agents · Computer Use

Support — Intercom Fin, Sierra:

- model classifies, drafts, decides escalation
- refund limits fixed by code → router ~ bounded loop

\vspace{2mm}

Computer use — Operator (2025), Anthropic computer use (2024):

- the tool surface is the screen: look, click, type

## Workflow Patterns

| Pattern | Returns in |
|:--|:--|
| Prompt chaining | Ch. 7 planning |
| Routing | Ch. 8 retrieval |
| Parallelization | Ch. 2 self-consistency |
| Orchestrator–workers | Ch. 6 multi-agent |
| Evaluator–optimizer | Ch. 5 reflection |

## Patterns in Production

- Orchestrator–workers — Anthropic research: lead agent + parallel searchers
- Evaluator–optimizer — every coding agent's edit ↔ test cycle
- Router — support triage: bot vs. human
- Parallelization — "parallel thinking" premium tiers
- Prompt chaining — fixed document pipelines

## Form Factors

| Form | Example |
|:--|:--|
| Conversational | ChatGPT, Claude |
| Delegated | Deep Research, Devin |
| Embedded | Copilot, Cursor |
| Headless | a sub-agent inside an agent |

\vspace{2mm}

The chatbot is one form factor — not the definition.

## Adoption Criteria

An agent pays when:

- the path cannot be fixed in code beforehand
- the work crosses several tools, order unknown
- feedback on intermediate results improves the outcome

Otherwise: a workflow — cheaper, more stable.

\vspace{2mm}

**Hand over only as much autonomy as the task requires.** (→ Ch. 12)

## When Not to Build an Agent

- "Summarize every report, this exact format" — procedure never varies
- "Answer FAQs from this list" — single turn, nothing to iterate
- "Transfer money on request" — costly errors, no verification step

\vspace{2mm}

Default = workflow. **The agent must earn its place.**

## The Course, From the Deficit List

- cannot act → tools (3) · the loop (4)
- doesn't know when wrong → reflection & evaluation (5) · planning (7)
- outgrows one agent → multi-agent (6)
- knows nothing past cutoff → RAG (8) · memory (10)
- input grows without bound → context (9)
- procedures migrate into weights → reasoning models (11)
- capability multiplies cost → economics (12) · benchmarks (13)
- action = attack surface → security (14)

# Backup

## Term Sheet

- **LLM** — next-token generator; text in, text out
- **Control flow** — next action · repetition · termination
- **Workflow** — control flow fixed by code
- **Agent** — control flow decided by model output
- **Agent loop** — generate → interpret → execute → append → repeat
- **Autonomy** — how many decisions the model holds
- **Form factor** — how the system meets people

## Products by Autonomy Band

- Fixed pipeline — batch translation, digests
- Router — support triage (Fin, Sierra)
- Bounded loop — Claude Code, Cursor: edit–test under a cap
- Autonomous — Deep Research, Devin
- Computer use — Operator: autonomy with a GUI as the toolbox

## Deciding the Split — a Checklist

1. Can the procedure be written down in advance? → workflow
2. Any way to verify results? If not → lower the autonomy
3. Several tools, order unknown upfront? → agent territory
4. Cost of one failure? → sets the bound and the guardrails, in code

## Discussion Questions 4–5

4. Pick one agentic product you use. Its form factor? Its four components? One decision its model makes — one its code fixes?

5. Same model as chatbot and inside Deep Research. Weights identical — where does the added capability come from? Which components supply it?

Same model, same question:

- "23 apples, 20 used, 6 bought — answer only" → **27** (wrong)
- same question, worked solution demanded → 23−20=3, 3+6=9 → **9**
